content.value_statement: Notification integrations can mishandle recipients, credentials, retries, and delivery results. This skill guides WxPusher implementation and troubleshooting using project conventions, documented API behavior, and mock tests.
actual_capabilities: Guide standard POST and SPT integration with UID, Topic, or token-based recipient routing.
Explain credential storage, environment configuration, log redaction, and appToken versus SPT incident handling.
Guide validation of HTTP responses, top-level business codes, and individual recipient results.
Plan timeouts, bounded retries, duplicate prevention, and notification failure isolation.
Specify mock tests for routing, response failures, missing configuration, and character and UTF-8 byte limits.
Diagnose client and WeChat ClawBot delivery issues, including binding, activation, and channel restrictions.
limitations: Provides guidance and reference documentation, not a bundled notification client or executable integration scripts.
Live notifications require user-provided service configuration and authorization for the intended recipients, purpose, and frequency.
API acceptance does not guarantee delivery or reading, and service limits can change.
Does not support arbitrary WeChat friend or group messaging or provide a verified public SPT revocation method.

use_cases.title: Report scheduled task failures
use_cases.description: Add WxPusher failure alerts to an existing script with minimal configuration, bounded retries, and mock validation.

use_cases.title: Integrate backend event notifications
use_cases.description: Extend an existing notification service with recipient routing, partial-failure handling, and duplicate prevention.

use_cases.title: Diagnose deployment alert delivery
use_cases.description: Review protected CI secrets, response codes, subscriber settings, and channel restrictions without automatically sending live messages.

prompt_templates.title: Understand WxPusher setup
prompt_templates.prompt: I have selected WxPusher for a personal script. Explain standard POST versus SPT, required configuration, and recipient prerequisites without sending messages.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: choose a supported notification mode.

prompt_templates.title: Add task notifications
prompt_templates.prompt: Add WxPusher failure notifications to this Python task using existing project conventions. Use placeholder configuration and mock tests; do not send live messages.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: implement a focused project integration.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate missing WeChat notifications
prompt_templates.prompt: WxPusher accepts my messages, but WeChat receives nothing. Review redacted responses, recipient results, ClawBot binding, activation, and limits without live pushes.

prompt_templates.title: Design resilient queue delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Integrate WxPusher into our existing queue worker with per-target validation, bounded retries, deduplication, redacted logs, and mock failure tests. Preserve primary business outcomes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: handle asynchronous delivery and reliability requirements.

output_examples.input: Add WxPusher failure notifications to a scheduled task without sending a live test.
output: Implementation scope: a small notification adapter and a task failure trigger.
Configuration: application token and recipient variables documented with placeholders.
Validation scope: mock success, business failure, timeout, and missing configuration cases.
Live push status: no real notification is sent during development validation.

output_examples.input: Explain why an accepted WxPusher message may not appear in WeChat.
output: API acceptance creates a sending task; it does not confirm delivery or reading.
Inspect individual recipient results, then verify ClawBot binding, enablement, activation, and channel limits.
Do not resend repeatedly or switch recipients to bypass delivery restrictions.

best_practices: Reuse project configuration, HTTP clients, and notification interfaces; keep credentials in approved secret storage.
Prefer JSON POST, redact logs, and check both top-level and individual recipient business results.
Validate with mocks first; send live messages only within explicit authorization for recipients, purpose, and frequency.
anti_patterns: Treating HTTP 200 or task creation as proof that every recipient received or read the notification.
Committing credentials, logging full authenticated URLs, or copying personal data into notification bodies.
Retrying indefinitely, defaulting to broadcast when recipients are missing, or assuming an SPT can be revoked by rescanning.

faq.question: Can I use this skill with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The core workflow is documentation-based and uses available project tools rather than a required host-specific integration.

faq.question: Does the skill include a ready-to-run notification client?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions and references for implementing WxPusher through your existing language, HTTP client, configuration, and testing tools.

faq.question: What configuration do standard pushes require?
faq.answer: Standard pushes require an appToken, message content, and UID or Topic targets. SPT uses a separate token-based mode.

faq.question: Will development tests send real notifications?
faq.answer: No, not by default. Development uses mocks; live pushes require explicit authorization covering the intended recipients, purpose, and frequency.

faq.question: Can WxPusher send to any WeChat friend or group?
faq.answer: No. The documented ClawBot channel requires user binding and activation, supports text notifications, and has channel-specific limits.

faq.question: How should I handle a leaked SPT?
faq.answer: Stop sharing it and clean controlled copies. Public references do not verify revocation; contact WxPusher and do not assume rescanning invalidates it.
